\section[la tintorería]{la tintorería — the dry cleaner's}

\label{lesson:ES-C770-tintoreria}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the plumber, then the Spanish for the electrician.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la tintorería}
\textbf{la tintorería} — \textquotedblleft{}the dry cleaner's\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Llevo el traje a la tintorería porque no se puede lavar.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I take the suit to the dry cleaner's because it can't be washed.}
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{tintorería} is built on \emph{tintorero} 'a dyer', from \emph{tinto} 'dyed', which comes from Latin \emph{tīnctus}, the participle of \emph{tingere} 'to wet, to dye' (Lewis \& Short). Dry cleaners were first dyers.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la tintorería}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la tintorería}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{la tintorería}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for the plumber, then the Spanish for the electrician, then say \emph{la tintorería} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does la tintorería mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The dry cleaner's\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[el probador]{el probador — the fitting room}

\label{lesson:ES-C770-probador}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the electrician, then the Spanish for the dry cleaner's.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: el probador}
\textbf{el probador} — \textquotedblleft{}the fitting room\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Prefiero esta tienda porque los probadores son grandes.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I prefer this shop because the fitting rooms are big.}
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{probador} is built on \emph{probar} 'to try on', inherited from Latin \emph{probāre} 'to test, to prove' (Lewis \& Short), with the ending \emph{-dor}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{el probador}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{el probador}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{el probador}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for the electrician, then the Spanish for the dry cleaner's, then say \emph{el probador} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does el probador mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The fitting room\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[la ferretería]{la ferretería — the hardware shop}

\label{lesson:ES-C770-ferreteria}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the dry cleaner's, then the Spanish for the fitting room.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la ferretería}
\textbf{la ferretería} — \textquotedblleft{}the hardware shop\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Voy a la ferretería porque necesito tornillos.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I'm going to the hardware shop because I need screws.}
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{ferretería} is built on \emph{ferrete} 'a small piece of iron' with the ending \emph{-ería} (EtymDB). \emph{Ferrete} comes from Latin \emph{ferrum} 'iron', the word that gave \emph{hierro}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la ferretería}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la ferretería}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{la ferretería}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for the dry cleaner's, then the Spanish for the fitting room, then say \emph{la ferretería} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does la ferretería mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The hardware shop\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[la carnicería]{la carnicería — the butcher's}

\label{lesson:ES-C770-carniceria}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the fitting room, then the Spanish for the hardware shop.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la carnicería}
\textbf{la carnicería} — \textquotedblleft{}the butcher's\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Compro en esta carnicería porque la carne es muy buena.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I shop at this butcher's because the meat is very good.}
\end{quote}

\emph{El carnicero} is the butcher.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{carnicería} is built on \emph{carnicero} 'a butcher' with the ending \emph{-ería} (EtymDB). The root is \emph{carne}, which comes from Latin \emph{carō}, \emph{carnem} 'flesh'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la carnicería}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la carnicería}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{la carnicería}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for the fitting room, then the Spanish for the hardware shop, then say \emph{la carnicería} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does la carnicería mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The butcher's\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[la frutería]{la frutería — the greengrocer's, the fruit shop}

\label{lesson:ES-C770-fruteria}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the hardware shop, then the Spanish for the butcher's.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la frutería}
\textbf{la frutería} — \textquotedblleft{}the greengrocer's, the fruit shop\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Voy a la frutería de la esquina porque tiene fruta de temporada.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I go to the fruit shop on the corner because it has fruit in season.}
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{frutería} is built on \emph{fruta} with the ending \emph{-ería} (EtymDB). \emph{Fruta} comes from Late Latin \emph{frūcta}, from \emph{frūctus} 'produce, enjoyment'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la frutería}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{la frutería}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for the hardware shop, then the Spanish for the butcher's, then say \emph{la frutería} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
